title: Pins on the Pavement
transcript: A city maintenance office introduced a phone app for reporting potholes after crews complained that street names alone rarely told them where to stop. The first version recorded the phone's position automatically, but people often filed reports after reaching home. The next version let residents move the pin to the actual spot. It also showed existing reports nearby, which helped people recognize a pothole someone else had already logged. At the end of the trial, crews spent less time searching for reported damage. The repair schedule barely changed, though, because the city still had the same number of trucks and workers.

questions.prompt: What problem led the maintenance office to introduce the app?
options: Crews received reports for roads outside the city.
Residents had trouble describing the size of potholes.
Maintenance workers missed reports sent after office hours.
Street names gave crews too little information to locate the damage.
questions.answer: Street names gave crews too little information to locate the damage.
questions.explanation: 维修人员说，光有街名很难确定要在哪个位置停车查看。

questions.prompt: What does the trial suggest about the effect of better location information?
options: It led the city to assign more crews to road maintenance.
It made damage easier to find without substantially speeding up repairs.
It helped crews complete more repairs by changing their work schedules.
It mainly improved the city's ability to predict future road damage.
questions.answer: It made damage easier to find without substantially speeding up repairs.
questions.explanation: 找坑洞所花的时间减少了，但车辆和人手数量没变，维修进度也几乎没变。
